newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Nervous Belgian OLO market faces crunch times.
newsitem.headline: Nervous Belgian OLO market faces crunch times.

text.p: Belgian OLOs were quaking in their boots on Tuesday as nervousness spread about possible interest rate increases to counter a strong dollar and a strengthening U.S. economy, dealers said.
Prices continued in Monday's weaker vein and dealers said there were sufficient factors for players to stay on the sidelines for the next week or so:
- U.S. retail sales and production data; - an OLO exchange auction; - rumours of G7 action to support the mark and brake the dollar; - unfavourable chart patterns; - French budget news.
"For prices to recover, the dollar should weaken but I don't see that happening -- no interest rate rises, no intervention; Europe can't really afford that, nor can EMU," a trader said.

The market was "really dangerous, unless you are short." There were a few courageous souls who had bucked the trend over the past months and suffered for it, but who now saw some small gains emerging. Still, their short-covering would not turn the market around, he added.
He said next Monday's presentation of an audit of French public finances would be a key event for Belgian bonds since it would provide clues on the likely success of the EMU project.
Dollar strength, and mark weakness, were coming on top of budget problems in France and Germany, adding to the strain on credibility of the single currency project, dealers said.
Although there was talk of Bundesbank action to support the mark, "the German economy does not allow for higher rates nor does the German budget," a trader said.

Analyst Conrad Fieremans at Kredietbank said the rumours were weighing on the short end of the curve in Belgium and Germany, "spoiling the climate." Expectations of indicator reports from the U.S. showing a third quarter pick-up in growth would add to the upward pressure on rates.

There could be some pressure on the OLO market from today's exchange auction, but given the rise in market interest rates and the resulting increase in the cost of financing any purchases he did not expect it to be a major success.
The Treasury is offering longer dated paper against OLO 8 (9.25 pct, Aug 1997) and OLO 4 (9.25 pct, Jan 1998) BELG.

Fieremans said the OLO/Bund spread reflected uncertainty about how the Bundesbank would handle the mark's weakness and also the soft tone to the Belgian franc. The 10-year spread widened to nine basis points in early trade, later easing back to eight, unchanged from Monday's late levels.

Fieremans said, "This is not the level to get into the market," certainly not with the charts pointing to a deeper correction. Ten-year yields could "easily" rise to 5.75 percent. They were at 5.69 at 1020 GMT, up from 5.65 late on Monday BE286=. If the U.S. retail sales data disappointed, 5.80 percent could be seen.

The data, due at 1230 GMT, are forecast to show a month on month rise of 0.2 percent at the headline level and 0.5 percent ex-autos. Fieremans said a headline 0.5 percent increase could see "a quite drastic reaction."
